newsitem.title: USA: North Korea nuclear work to start soon - officials.
newsitem.headline: North Korea nuclear work to start soon - officials.

text.p: Preparatatory work will begin within weeks at the site where two nuclear reactors will be built in North Korea by the Pyongyang government and an international consortium, officials said on Wednesday.

The officials from North Korea and the Korean Peninsula Energy Development Organisation (KEDO), which includes the United States, Japan and South Korea, made the announcement in New York when they signed technical and policy agreements required to prepare the site.

The light-water reactor project has been negotiated by KEDO and Pyongyang over two years following a deal signed in Geneva in 1994 between Washington and Pyongyang. The isolationist Stalinist state agreed to freeze and ultimately dismantle its existing nuclear programme, which the West suspected was being used to develop nuclear weapons.

"This is the end of the formal negotiations on the issues that we have to resolve before we can begin work," KEDO executive director Stephen Bosworth told a news conference. "I think that the difficult issues are really now behind us, now it's more a question of keeping the momentum of the project going forward."
Bosworth said the site preparation work would begin "within weeks" while North Korean ambassador-at-large Ho Jong said he expected the work to start in early August.

Under the $4.5 billion Geneva deal, Washington promised Pyongyang two light-water reactors generating 1,000 megawatts of power each by approximately 2003. North Korea was assured interim energy in the form of 500,000 metric tons of of heavy fuel per year for heating and electricity.
